operation_details.item: The user does not want SEO keywords, search-optimized headings, or meta descriptions in marketing copy drafts.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Morning! How's the marketing copy draft coming along? I saw you were working on it earlier.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Morning! It's mostly done, but I'm already dreading the inevitable requests to stuff in SEO keywords and tweak the headings for search. It always messes with the flow.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Ah, the classic SEO tug-of-war. Is your client pushing hard for that?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: They haven't yet, but I know they will. For me, the ideal draft just reads naturally. No keyword stuffing, no 'search-optimized' headings, no meta description gymnastics. Just clear, engaging prose.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That sounds like a pretty consistent writing philosophy for you. Do you usually write the first draft that way and then adjust if the client insists?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. I always start clean. If they want me to butcher it with keyword lists afterward, that's a separate conversation. But I'd rather never have to think about SEO at the drafting stage.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Got it. So for this draft, I'll make sure we keep it natural and don't force any SEO elements in. Just focus on the story and the reader.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Thanks, that's a relief. I'll send you the draft later today for a quick read-through. If anything looks optimized to death, you know I'll reject it.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Ha, I'll keep an eye out. Looking forward to reading it. Let me know when it's ready.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Will do. Have a good one!

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that I do not want SEO keywords, headings optimized for search, or meta descriptions in any marketing copy I ask you to draft.
